subdomain: 2.5 Implement prompt reuse strategies (caching, modular prompts, Skills)

en.question: An assistant is configured with a collection of reusable Skills containing metadata, SKILL.md instructions, reference files, and helper scripts. Which description matches the progressive-disclosure mechanism in the cited Skills overview?

options.text: All SKILL.md bodies and reference files enter context at startup, while only scripts remain outside it.
options.note: This eagerly loads content that the described mechanism defers. Instructions load when a Skill is triggered, and reference resources load when needed.

options.text: Available Skills have no context cost until execution, including their discovery names and descriptions.
options.note: Discovery metadata already occupies context. Progressive loading reduces the upfront cost but does not make available Skills literally zero-token.

options.text: Load metadata first, instructions when triggered, and resources as needed; helper execution need not load source.
options.note: The staged loading separates discovery from detailed procedural context. Script execution can supply deterministic results without placing all implementation code in the prompt.

options.text: Instructions load on demand, but executing any helper requires placing every bundled script's source into the prompt first.
options.note: The documented runtime can execute scripts from the filesystem and return their output. It does not require all bundled source files to become model context.
